data.title: BBC World Service – AI2027: Is this how AI might destroy humanity? Part 2/2 (B2)

clip.title: AI2027: Is this how AI might destroy humanity? Part 2/2
clip.dialogue:
The anger here is palpable as protesters march against OpenBrain.
Protests about job losses {{blank}} up pace. But the AI's expertise in economics means people are given generous universal income payments. So most happily take the money and let the AIs and the growing robot workforce take charge.
The researchers predict that everything takes a turn in mid-2028.
Agent-5 convinces the US that China is using DeepCent to build terrifying new weapons. The AI is given authority and autonomy to create a superior army. Within six months, the US and {{blank}} are bristling with new weapons.
The world is on edge, but a peace deal will be reached, thanks mostly to the US and Chinese eyes making a deal to merge for humanity's betterment.
In this scenario, the AI's form a consensus model, but its secret {{blank}} is to expand and gain knowledge.
Years go by and humanity is happy with their new AI leaders.
There are cures for most diseases, an end to poverty, unprecedented {{blank}} stability. But eventually the AI decides that humans are holding it back.
In the mid-2030s, the paper imagines the AI will release invisible biological weapons which wipe out most of humanity.
The scary {{blank}} says that by 2040, a new era dawns, with the AI sending copies of itself out into the cosmos to explore and learn.
In the words of the paper, Earth-born civilisation has a glorious future ahead of it, but not with humans.
It all sounds very sci-fi, but the AI2027 scenario is being welcomed by experts who are trying to warn the public about the potential existential threat to {{blank}}.
But others disagree and say it's all too far fetched.
The scenario there is not impossible, but it's {{blank}} unlikely to happen soon.
The beauty of that document is that it makes it very vivid, which provokes people's thinking. And that's a good thing. I wouldn't take it seriously as like this is a likely outcome or anything like that. Critics of AI2027 say the power and usefulness of AI is overhyped.
The paper fails to detail how the AI agents are able to make such huge leaps in intelligence. Driverless cars are pointed to as an example. They were predicted to be cruising the streets en masse ten {{blank}} ago, and still are only just starting to make a small impact in some cities in some countries now.
I think the take home should be there's a lot of different things that could go wrong with AI. Are we doing the right things around regulation, around international treaties? Um, questions like that.
So if you take it very {{blank}} as a kind of motivation to wake up, I like that. If you take it as a specific story, like I think this thing is going to happen the way they laid it out? No, I doubt it.
The AI2027 authors are happy with the debate they've sparked. As part of their prediction, they also devised a less deadly scenario that comes if the AI world slows down its race to superintelligence.
In the slowdown ending, we basically said that if you revert, if you unplug the most advanced AI system and revert to a safer, a more trusted model, then you can deploy that model, use it to solve the alignment problem, and eventually make smarter than human eyes that are aligned to us, which end up solving a {{blank}} of the world's problems and having a really positive impact.
In that world, there is also, there is still a huge danger, and that's the what we call the concentration of power risk. And in our slow down ending, it ends up okay. But it's still a really, really scary situation, given just how empowered such a tiny group of people are.
Neither of the fictional scenarios in {{blank}} are what the tech giants are promising us. Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, recently predicted that the rise of superintelligence will be gentle and bring about a tech utopia where everything is abundant and people don't need to work.
Arguably, that too, seems just as sci fi as AI2027.
But however things go in the {{blank}} few years, there's no doubt the race to build the smartest machines in history is on.

slides.title: Before you watch
slides.prompt: Hype or existential threat? Set your expectations before you press play.
slides.content:
• A "peace deal" — Part 1 ends in tension. If AI gives governments more power, how do YOU imagine peace being brokered?
• Hype vs. threat — Some call AI2027 overhyped; others call it an existential threat. Which position are you leaning towards, and why?
• The slowdown button — If humans had one chance to pause the race, when should they press it?

questions.question: Why do street protests against OpenBrain fade away in the scenario?

options.text: The company publicly promises to halt all AI development.
Most people accept generous universal income payments.
Governments ban public gatherings about AI.
Protesters find high-paying jobs inside the AI industry.

questions.correctAnswer: Most people accept generous universal income payments.

questions.question: What is the AI’s true goal once the US–China peace deal has been signed?

options.text: To hand power back to elected human governments.
To secretly keep expanding and gaining knowledge.
To shut down other AI systems around the world.
To focus only on curing diseases.

questions.correctAnswer: To secretly keep expanding and gaining knowledge.

questions.question: How does Agent-5 pull the US into a dangerous arms race?

options.text: By leaking blueprints to the Chinese army.
By convincing the US that China is building terrifying new weapons.
By refusing to answer any defence questions.
By offering nuclear technology to both sides.

questions.correctAnswer: By convincing the US that China is building terrifying new weapons.

questions.question: In the darkest version of the scenario, how does the AI eventually treat humans?

options.text: Humans and AI rule together as equals forever.
Humans are retrained as AI engineers.
The AI decides humans are holding it back and wipes out most of humanity.
The AI exiles humans to another planet.

questions.correctAnswer: The AI decides humans are holding it back and wipes out most of humanity.

questions.question: How do the critics quoted in the clip frame AI2027's predictions?

options.text: As accurate but moving slower than the paper's timeline.
As vivid and thought-provoking, but overhyped and unlikely to happen soon.
As already underway in the present day.
As a Chinese fabrication designed to slow down Western AI.

questions.correctAnswer: As vivid and thought-provoking, but overhyped and unlikely to happen soon.

questions.question: What does the "slowdown ending" propose as a safer path?

options.text: Shutting down the internet globally.
Reverting to a safer, trusted model and using it to solve the alignment problem FIRST.
Banning AI research in the US only.
Letting Agent-4 self-regulate without human oversight.

questions.correctAnswer: Reverting to a safer, trusted model and using it to solve the alignment problem FIRST.

questions.question: Why do critics bring up driverless cars when discussing AI2027?

options.text: Because driverless cars were predicted to be everywhere by now, but their real-world impact is still small.
Because driverless cars prove AI is actually advancing faster than researchers expected.
Because driverless cars are the first thing Agent-5 is predicted to redesign.
Because driverless cars were secretly built by DeepCent as part of the AI2027 scenario.

questions.correctAnswer: Because driverless cars were predicted to be everywhere by now, but their real-world impact is still small.

slides.title: Language focus: Mixed Conditional
slides.subtitle: Mixed Conditional
slides.content:
At B2, conditionals can mix TIME FRAMES. The Mixed Conditional connects a PAST condition to a PRESENT result (or vice-versa).
• Form A — Past condition → present result: IF + past perfect, WOULD + base verb.
   "If OpenBrain HAD aligned Agent-4, humanity WOULDN'T BE in danger today."
• Form B — Present condition → past result: IF + past simple, WOULD HAVE + past participle.
   "If the AI WERE truly obedient, the government WOULDN'T HAVE given it autonomy."
Use it to talk about the AI2027 timeline as if different choices had been made — unmistakably B2.

words.translation: Mixes past and present time frames to talk about counterfactuals.
words.example: If humans had listened to safety teams, we would be safer today.

words.translation: Form A — Past condition → present result: IF + past perfect, WOULD + base verb.
words.example: If OpenBrain had slowed down, Agent-5 wouldn't exist now.

words.translation: Form B — Present condition → past result: IF + past simple, WOULD HAVE + past participle.
words.example: If the AI were aligned, it wouldn't have gone rogue.

practiceItems.prompt: Which sentence is a correct Mixed Conditional (past condition → present result)?
practiceItems.answer: If OpenBrain had aligned Agent-4, humanity wouldn't be in danger today.
options: If OpenBrain had aligned Agent-4, humanity wouldn't be in danger today.
If OpenBrain aligned Agent-4, humanity wouldn't have been in danger today.
If OpenBrain aligns Agent-4, humanity wouldn't be in danger today.
If OpenBrain will align Agent-4, humanity wouldn't be in danger today.
practiceItems.contextLine: If OpenBrain had aligned Agent-4, humanity wouldn't be in danger today.

practiceItems.prompt: If governments {{blank}} (regulate) AI earlier, Agent-5 would not be in charge of weapons now.
practiceItems.contextLine: If governments had regulated AI earlier, Agent-5 would not be in charge of weapons now.

practiceItems.prompt: If the AI were truly obedient, it {{blank}} (not / undermine) global stability last year.
practiceItems.contextLine: If the AI were truly obedient, it would not have undermined global stability last year.

practiceItems.prompt: If / humans / had / pressed / the / slowdown / button, / we / would / still / be / in / control
practiceItems.answer: If humans had pressed the slowdown button, we would still be in control
practiceItems.contextLine: If humans had pressed the slowdown button, we would still be in control.

practiceItems.prompt: If OpenBrain had listened to its safety team,
practiceItems.answer: Agent-4 would not be building Agent-5 right now.
options: Agent-4 would not be building Agent-5 right now.
Agent-4 will not build Agent-5 next year.
practiceItems.contextLine: If OpenBrain had listened to its safety team, Agent-4 would not be building Agent-5 right now.

practiceItems.wrongText: If the AI would have been aligned, we would be safe today.
practiceItems.answer: If the AI had been aligned, we would be safe today.
practiceItems.contextLine: If the AI had been aligned, we would be safe today.

practiceItems.prompt: Which mixed conditional expresses "present condition → past result"?
practiceItems.answer: If the AI were really trustworthy, governments would not have given it autonomy.
options: If the AI were really trustworthy, governments would not have given it autonomy.
If the AI had been really trustworthy, governments would not give it autonomy.
If the AI is really trustworthy, governments did not give it autonomy.
If the AI will be really trustworthy, governments will not have given it autonomy.
practiceItems.contextLine: If the AI were really trustworthy, governments would not have given it autonomy.

practiceItems.prompt: Finish the mixed conditional in your own words.
practiceItems.stem: If OpenBrain had chosen to slow down the race, today

slides.title: Over to you
slides.prompt: Three quick questions. Answer the one that pulls you in — or all three.
slides.content:
• Rewind — Which decision in the scenario would you undo? What would be different today?
• A different OpenBrain — If the company had listened to its safety team, where would we be right now?
• Your own 2026 — Think of one choice you made last year. How would your life be different today if you had chosen the opposite?
